questions.stem: The post-election wave of party-switching by MPs has renewed focus on India's anti-defection law. Consider the following statements regarding the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Tenth Schedule was inserted into the Constitution by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
A merger of a legislative party with another party is exempted from disqualification only if at least two-thirds of its members agree to the merger.
A decision on disqualification of a Member of Parliament under the Tenth Schedule is taken by the President of India.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985. Statement 2 is correct — the two-thirds merger exemption was retained even after the 91st Amendment (2003) removed the one-third 'split' exemption. Statement 3 is incorrect — the Speaker (Lok Sabha) or Chairman (Rajya Sabha) decides disqualification petitions, not the President.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: The story of India's post-election defection wave since 2022, in charts
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Tenth Schedule/anti-defection law (52nd Amendment, 1985) and the Speaker's adjudicatory role, a recurring Prelims theme.

questions.stem: Indian companies are preparing for a new financial reporting standard, Ind AS 118. With reference to Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) in general, which one of the following best describes them?
options: They are tax accounting standards notified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes for computation of taxable income under the Income Tax Act.
They are accounting standards converged with IFRS, notified by the Central Government under the Companies Act, 2013 in consultation with the National Financial Reporting Authority.
They are prudential accounting norms prescribed exclusively for public sector banks by the Reserve Bank of India.
They are voluntary disclosure norms framed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India for listed companies' quarterly results.
questions.explanation: Ind AS are India's accounting standards converged with International Financial Reporting Standards, notified by the Central Government under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 in consultation with the NFRA. Option (a) confuses Ind AS with the separate Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS) under the Income Tax Act; (c) wrongly restricts them to banks regulated by RBI; (d) wrongly attributes them to SEBI's disclosure regime.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Ind AS 118: India Inc gears up for big changes to financial reporting
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional framework of accounting standard-setting in India, similar in format to UPSC 2019's 'which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?'

questions.stem: India has set a target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity by 2030. Consider the following statements in this regard:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity target by 2030 was announced as part of India's 'Panchamrit' commitments at the COP26 summit in Glasgow.
Non-fossil fuel capacity, as used for this target, includes solar, wind, nuclear and large hydro power.
The Central Electricity Authority is a statutory body that undertakes power system planning under the Electricity Act, 2003.
Battery energy storage systems are themselves classified as a source of renewable energy generation under India's power sector framework.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the 500 GW target was part of the Panchamrit commitments at COP26 (2021); non-fossil capacity includes nuclear and large hydro besides renewables; and the CEA is a statutory planning body under the Electricity Act, 2003. Statement 4 is incorrect — battery storage is a storage technology that supports grid integration of renewables, it is not itself classified as a generation source.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: 500 GW by 2030: Experts explain why India needs to power up battery storage capacity and grid infra to meet the target
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's climate/energy commitments and the non-fossil fuel capacity target, an area UPSC has tested via India's COP26 pledges.

questions.stem: With reference to the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, consider the following pairs of terms and their descriptions:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: The individual to whom the personal data relates
The entity that determines the purpose and means of processing personal data
A government body empowered to penalize data breaches
An adjudicatory body established under the Act to enforce its provisions
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched. Pair 3 is incorrect — a Consent Manager under the DPDP Act is a registered, accountable entity through which a data principal gives, manages, reviews and withdraws consent; it is not a government body with penalising powers. That enforcement and penalty function belongs to the Data Protection Board of India.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: India needs to train its clinical staff before erecting data shields
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional architecture of the DPDP Act, 2023, in the pairs-matching format UPSC has increasingly used for digital governance topics.

questions.stem: The Centre has extended the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme until 31 March 2027. Consider the following statements about the scheme:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund was launched in 2020 as a central sector scheme with a total fund size of Rs 1 lakh crore.
Under the scheme, an interest subvention of 4 per cent per annum is available on eligible loans up to Rs 1 crore.
The scheme is administered by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
Eligible beneficiaries under the scheme include Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, Farmer Producer Organisations and agri-entrepreneurs.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct — the AIF was launched in 2020 with a Rs 1 lakh crore corpus, and PACS, FPOs and agri-entrepreneurs are eligible beneficiaries. Statement 2 is incorrect — the actual interest subvention is 3 per cent per annum on loans up to Rs 2 crore. Statement 3 is incorrect — the scheme is administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Centre extends AIF scheme to boost farm infrastructure investments
questions.pyqLink: Tests design features of central agricultural credit/infrastructure schemes, a recurring Prelims area alongside PM-KISAN and PM-FME type schemes.

questions.stem: India's crude oil imports from the Middle East have risen with shipments moving through key maritime chokepoints. With reference to one such chokepoint, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and lies between Iran and Oman.
The Strait of Malacca, not the Strait of Hormuz, is the principal maritime chokepoint for India's crude oil imports from the Middle East.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Strait of Hormuz, bounded by Iran and the Musandam peninsula of Oman, links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. Statement 2 is incorrect — the Strait of Hormuz, not Malacca, is the critical chokepoint for Middle East-origin crude bound for India; the Strait of Malacca is primarily significant for India's and East Asia's trade with the Pacific region.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: India's Mideast oil imports return to pre-war levels in September
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of global maritime chokepoints/straits, an area UPSC has tested via questions on the Strait of Malacca and similar straits.

questions.stem: In the context of France's current debt and political crisis, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The spread between French and German 10-year government bond yields is widely used as a gauge of sovereign credit risk within the Eurozone.
Statement-II: Germany's sovereign bonds (Bunds) are regarded as the Eurozone's benchmark 'safe asset' owing to the country's strong fiscal position and credit rating.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I: because German Bunds are treated as the Eurozone's risk-free benchmark, the yield spread of other members' bonds (like France's OATs) over Bunds directly reflects the market's perception of that country's relative sovereign credit risk — exactly the widening seen amid France's fiscal and political unrest.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: France's debt crisis explained: Could it trigger another euro zone meltdown?
questions.pyqLink: Tests sovereign bond spread mechanics and Eurozone fiscal architecture, using the Statement-I/II format UPSC introduced from 2022 for economy-linked questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the institutional architecture of India's space sector:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Department of Space is administered directly under the Prime Minister's Office.
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) functions as the executing agency of the Department of Space.
IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) is the single-window nodal agency authorising private sector participation in space activities.
NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the Department of Space is under the direct charge of the Prime Minister (with a Minister of State assisting), ISRO is its executing arm, and IN-SPACe is the nodal single-window body authorising and promoting private players. Statement 4 is wrong — NSIL is a Central Public Sector Enterprise incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013, not a statutory body created by Parliament.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: How poor education, training infra constrains India's military space plans
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional set-up of India's space sector (Dept of Space/ISRO/IN-SPACe/NSIL), a recurring static theme since UPSC began asking about space reforms post-2020.

questions.stem: With reference to Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) data reported by the Reserve Bank of India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Net FDI is calculated as gross FDI inflows minus total FDI outflows, including outward FDI by Indian companies and repatriation by foreign companies.
India recorded positive net FDI for five consecutive months between August and December 2025.
The Reserve Bank of India publishes data on India's FDI flows through its monthly Bulletin.
In August 2026, outward investment by Indian companies was the main driver of total FDI outflows, exceeding repatriation by foreign firms.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — net FDI nets out gross inflows against both outward investment and repatriation, and the RBI reports this data through its monthly Bulletin. Statement 2 is wrong: the article records five consecutive months of negative (not positive) net FDI during August–December 2025. Statement 4 is wrong: in August 2026 the outflow was driven mainly by repatriation by foreign companies, not outward investment by Indian firms.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Net FDI at $3.3 billion in September 2026, positive for third consecutive month
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Balance of Payments concept of gross vs net FDI and the RBI's role as data publisher, similar to UPSC's recurring BoP-component questions.

questions.stem: With reference to India's bilateral diplomatic arrangements, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A 'Strategic Partnership' between India and a foreign country is a legally binding treaty that requires ratification by Parliament.
India and Poland elevated their bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership during a Prime Ministerial visit to Warsaw in 2024.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct — the article confirms India-Poland ties were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during PM Modi's August 2024 visit to Warsaw. Statement 1 is wrong: a 'Strategic Partnership' is a diplomatic/political designation of close cooperation, not a legally binding treaty requiring parliamentary ratification; it has no fixed status under international law.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India-Poland strategic partnership should translate into JVs: PM Donald Tusk
questions.pyqLink: Tests the nature of 'Strategic Partnership' as a diplomatic category (distinct from a treaty), a recurring distractor in IR questions on India's bilateral frameworks.

questions.stem: A Minister's written reply in the Lok Sabha, as cited regarding Department of Space vacancies, is part of India's Parliamentary Question mechanism. Consider the following statements about this mechanism:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A Starred Question requires an oral answer on the floor of the House and permits supplementary questions.
An Unstarred Question requires only a written reply and does not permit supplementary questions.
A Short Notice Question can be asked with less than the normal notice period, but only with the prior permission of the Speaker or Chairman.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct: Starred Questions get oral answers with scope for supplementaries; Unstarred Questions get only written replies with no supplementaries; and Short Notice Questions, on urgent public matters, bypass the usual notice period only with the Speaker's/Chairman's prior consent.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: How poor education, training infra constrains India's military space plans
questions.pyqLink: Tests the classification of Parliamentary Questions (starred/unstarred/short notice), a staple static polity topic frequently tested via Lok Sabha procedure questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of crude oil benchmarks and their associated description:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Benchmark priced off North Sea (UK/Norway) oilfields
Benchmark priced off onshore oilfields in the United States
Benchmark used for sour crude exported from the Persian Gulf to Asia
Derived solely from India's domestic crude oil production
questions.explanation: The first three pairs are correctly matched — Brent (North Sea), WTI (US onshore), and Dubai/Oman (Gulf sour crude benchmark for Asia) are all accurately described. The fourth pair is wrong: India's crude oil basket is a weighted average of Dubai/Oman (sour) and Brent (sweet) import prices, since India imports roughly 85% of its crude — it does not reflect domestic production.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Oil prices extend rally to near six-month high amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
questions.pyqLink: Tests the geography of global crude oil benchmarks and the composition of India's import-based crude basket, relevant to questions on petroleum geography and energy security.

questions.stem: With reference to the obituary of physicist Claude Cohen-Tannoudji, which mentions his links to Indian physics, which one of the following best describes the 'Pancharatnam-Berry phase'?
options: A geometric phase acquired by a quantum system when its parameters are varied cyclically and adiabatically, first identified by Indian physicist S. Pancharatnam in the context of polarised light interference.
A nuclear energy-level splitting effect discovered by S. Pancharatnam while studying crystal optics at the Raman Research Institute.
A classical mechanical resonance effect explaining planetary orbital precession, derived jointly by Pancharatnam and Michael Berry.
A thermodynamic law governing phase transitions in superconductors cooled near absolute zero.
questions.explanation: The Pancharatnam-Berry phase (also called the geometric phase) describes a phase shift a quantum system acquires under cyclic, adiabatic change of its parameters — first worked out by S. Pancharatnam for polarised light interference in 1956, and later generalised by Michael Berry in 1984. The other options misattribute it to nuclear physics, orbital mechanics, or superconductivity, none of which the concept concerns.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: A physicist who took atoms near absolute zero, and physics further
questions.pyqLink: Tests awareness of lesser-known Indian contributions to modern physics (S. Pancharatnam's geometric phase), in the spirit of UPSC's 'personalities and their contributions' questions.

questions.stem:
With reference to a recent study on urban building clusters and surface temperature, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Grouping buildings with similar functions into larger contiguous clusters within a city can lower local surface urban heat island intensity.
Statement-II: Buildings with similar functions tend to have comparable shapes and operating schedules, which allows better airflow and more coordinated heat release.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: The study found that every 100-metre increase in functional cluster scale reduced urban heat island intensity by 4.5%, precisely because buildings with similar functions share comparable shapes and operating schedules, enabling better airflow and coordinated heat release — making Statement-II the correct explanation for Statement-I.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Science Snapshots: October 25, 2026
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static ecological concept of the Urban Heat Island effect and its mitigation through urban form, a recurring Environment theme tied to city planning and climate resilience.

questions.stem: The Union government has proposed changes to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) to capture gig and unpaid household work. In this context, consider the following statements about the PLFS. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
The Unemployment Rate under PLFS is estimated using both the Usual Status approach and the Current Weekly Status approach.
PLFS provides quarterly employment estimates for rural areas and only annual estimates for urban areas.
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) and Worker Population Ratio (WPR) are key indicators generated through the PLFS.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: PLFS is run by NSSO under MoSPI, uses both Usual Status and Current Weekly Status to estimate unemployment, and generates LFPR/WPR/UR as its core indicators. Statement 3 is reversed — PLFS gives quarterly estimates for urban areas only, with both rural and urban annual estimates, not the other way round.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Government to modify labour survey to capture gig economy, unpaid household workers
questions.pyqLink: Tests PLFS design/indicators, a recurring static theme (cf. UPSC 2021 prelims question on NSSO employment survey methodology).

questions.stem: The Vadodara Municipal Corporation's Standing Committee approved a land allotment that must now be ratified by the General Board. With reference to the institutional structure of Urban Local Bodies in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Standing Committee of a Municipal Corporation is a body constitutionally mandated by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, distinct from Ward Committees.
The General Board (Council) of a Municipal Corporation is its highest legislative and decision-making body, and executive decisions of the Standing Committee typically require its ratification.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct — the General Board is the apex elected, decision-making body of a Municipal Corporation, and Standing Committee resolutions generally go to it for ratification. Statement 1 is incorrect: the 74th CAA mandates Ward Committees (Article 243S) for corporations above a population threshold, but Standing/Executive Committees are creatures of state municipal legislation, not a direct constitutional mandate.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: On what basis has the Gujarat government ‘gifted’ a plot to Yusuf Pathan?
questions.pyqLink: Tests 74th Constitutional Amendment Act structure of urban local bodies (cf. UPSC prelims questions on Ward Committees and Municipalities, Article 243Q-243S).

questions.stem: Troops faced off in Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri district near the Line of Actual Control (LAC). With reference to the India-China boundary, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The LAC in Arunachal Pradesh broadly corresponds to the Eastern Sector of the India-China boundary, aligned roughly along the McMahon Line.
The McMahon Line was demarcated through the Shimla Convention of 1914 between British India and China, and China formally recognises it as the boundary.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the Eastern Sector covering Arunachal Pradesh is delineated roughly along the McMahon Line. Statement 2 is wrong on two counts: the Shimla Convention (1914) was between British India and Tibet (China did not ratify it), and China explicitly rejects the McMahon Line and the Convention's validity.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: India-China face-off in Arunachal: What lies behind the border tensions
questions.pyqLink: Tests the three sectors of the India-China boundary and the McMahon Line (cf. UPSC prelims questions on Himalayan boundary disputes and the Shimla Convention).

questions.stem: The latest ethanol procurement tender has raised feedstock concerns among grain-based producers. With reference to India's ethanol blending policy, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, ethanol can be produced from sugarcane juice/molasses as well as from surplus foodgrains such as maize and rice, both classified as first-generation (1G) biofuel sources.
The National Policy on Biofuels permits the use of foodgrains unfit for human consumption (damaged foodgrains) as a feedstock for ethanol production.
India achieved its 20% ethanol blending (E20) target strictly according to the original 2030 timeline set out in the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018.
none
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — both sugar-based and grain-based (including damaged foodgrains) feedstocks are permitted 1G ethanol sources under the EBP programme. Statement 3 is incorrect because India achieved the E20 target well ahead of the original 2030 timeline (by 2025-26), not 'strictly according to' it.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Ethanol tender sparks feedstock concerns as rice gains ground over maize
questions.pyqLink: Tests classification of biofuel generations and the National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 (cf. UPSC 2020 prelims question on types of biofuels and their feedstocks).

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of economic reports/surveys and the body responsible for releasing them. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
questions.explanation: PLFS-NSSO/MoSPI, WPI-Office of Economic Adviser/DPIIT, and the RBI Bulletin's 'State of the Economy' article-RBI are all correctly matched. The third pair is wrong: the headline Consumer Price Index is released by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI, not the Labour Bureau, which instead publishes the separate CPI-Industrial Workers and CPI-Agricultural Labourers series.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Data suggests broad-based increase in food prices: RBI Bulletin
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional ownership of key economic indices, a frequent UPSC pattern (cf. UPSC 2023 prelims pairs-matched question on reports and publishing bodies).

questions.stem: A proposed amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 would allow the government to notify a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above a threshold value. Which one of the following best describes the term 'Merchant Discount Rate'?
options: The fee charged by card networks to banks for providing interoperability across ATM networks
The fee that a merchant pays to a bank or payment service provider for facilitating an electronic payment transaction, usually charged as a percentage of the transaction value
The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India discounts bills of exchange presented by commercial banks
The statutory discount a retailer is required to offer on the Maximum Retail Price for payments made through digital modes
questions.explanation: MDR is the charge a merchant pays an acquiring bank/payment service provider for processing an electronic payment, typically a small percentage of transaction value; UPI has so far operated under a zero-MDR regime. Option A describes ATM interchange, option C describes the Bank Rate, and option D describes no real regulatory requirement.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: UPI and the cost of policy reversal
questions.pyqLink: Directly mirrors UPSC 2019 prelims: 'Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?'
